core: Debt, equity, dilution, repayment, control, and risk concepts
supporting: Customer revenue as a source of operating cash
U.S. securities-law caveat for real equity transactions

claims.claim: The SBA groups self-funding, investors, and loans among ways a U.S. business may fund itself and says financing needs are not one-size-fits-all.
Debt financing is borrowing that must be repaid under its terms, while equity financing exchanges capital for an ownership interest; these have different cash-flow and ownership consequences.
Grant eligibility and permitted use are determined by the specific funding opportunity and its legal instructions rather than a general label of grant.
In the United States, offers and sales of securities by private companies must be registered or made pursuant to an available exemption under federal securities law.
A founder holding 100 of 125 total ownership units holds 80 percent, demonstrating percentage dilution after a new issuance in a purely hypothetical example.

sourceRecords.title: Fund your business
sourceRecords.notes: Read live. Supports the broad U.S. framing of self-funding, investor capital, loans, crowdfunding, and program-based funding, together with the control and risk trade-off of self-funding. Used only for original general education; no individual funding path is recommended.

sourceRecords.notes: Read live. Supports the high-level distinction between debt repayment and equity ownership, varied financing sources, and the different cash-flow implications. Used only for original synthesis; no source prose adapted.

sourceRecords.title: Grant Eligibility
sourceRecords.notes: Read live. Supports the point that federal grant eligibility depends on the particular opportunity and applicant category. Used only for a jurisdiction-qualified eligibility caveat, not as grant-application advice.

sourceRecords.title: Private Companies and the SEC
sourceRecords.notes: Read live. Supports the narrow U.S. legal caveat that private-company security offers and sales are regulated, including transactions involving friends, family, angel investors, and venture funds. This lesson does not provide offering, solicitation, or compliance instructions.
